items.title: Centre plans incentives for wider adoption of induction cookstoves
items.summary: Policymakers see induction cookstoves as a way to reduce exposure to global LPG supply disruptions for its 340 million consumers. They also estimate that induction cooking costs about a third less than conventional cooking methods.

items.title: India’s metal exports ride global electrification wave
items.summary: India's exports of key metal intermediates are experiencing a significant surge. Aluminium alloy exports climbed twenty-four percent, reaching one point two nine billion dollars. Insulated copper winding wire exports accelerated fifty-eight percent, with the United States as a leading destination. Refined lead exports also rose fifty-six percent, driven by Asian market demand. These gains reflect India's growing integration into global manufacturing supply chains.

items.title: Indian manufacturers turn to air freight as West Asia crisis disrupts sea shipments
items.summary: Indian manufacturers are airlifting components to ensure festive season production continuity. Sea freight delays and congestion are making ocean shipping unreliable for these companies. Air freight costs are significantly higher, but timely supplies are crucial for demand. Companies are absorbing some increased costs to avoid impacting sales recovery. Logistics partners are exploring innovative routes to manage ongoing disruptions.

Meanwhile, a dip in oil prices, influenced by advancing peace talks, helped to soothe inflation fears.

items.title: Government explores incentives for polysilicon manufacturing to boost solar energy production
items.summary: The government is exploring a new incentive scheme for polysilicon manufacturing. This initiative aims to bolster domestic production capabilities within the sector. Currently, a production-linked incentive scheme supports solar module manufacturing. That program covers modules, cells, ingot-wafers, and polysilicon production. This new exploration follows earlier discussions on supporting polysilicon manufacturing.

items.title: High on India growth, Diageo gives region 'Standalone' tag
items.summary: Diageo is taking a bold step by designating India as a distinct operational region, separating it from the Asia-Pacific hub. This strategic choice is driven by the projected growth in India's spirits market. In tandem, the company is revamping its packaging network for Indian spirits, which is set to yield significant and recurring cost savings.

items.title: Instant home services firms Urban Company, Snabbit slash prices, cut waiting times as competition intensifies
items.summary: The sector's rising cash burn, coupled with the relatively limited size of the addressable market, is beginning to concern investors tracking the space. The category is economically viable primarily in urban catchments, where high order density supports efficient fulfilment and worker utilisation. Expanding into lower-density neighbourhoods is significantly more challenging, another industry executive said.

items.title: Renewable energy bid discovers record low tariff of ₹5.25 per unit in SECI tender
items.summary: A competitive tariff of ₹5.25 per unit was discovered for round-the-clock renewable energy. This price emerged from a tender by the Solar Energy Corporation of India. The discovered tariff aims to compare with firm power sources like thermal and nuclear. Renewable energy must be supplied reliably on a round-the-clock basis. This development highlights the growing competitiveness of renewable energy sources.

items.title: PFRDA approves four new pension funds, increasing total to 14 for NPS subscribers
items.summary: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority has approved four new pension funds. This expansion aims to increase non-government NPS subscribers significantly over five years. Digital initiatives are expected to attract millions of new subscribers annually. PFRDA emphasises accessibility and simplified onboarding for broader pension coverage. Conservative schemes have delivered strong annual returns, building on past successes.

items.title: AWL Agri business penalised for substandard O=oil
items.summary: FSSAI has secured an order against AWL Agri Business for substandard fortified sunflower oil. Laboratory tests found the product failed to meet prescribed vitamin fortification standards. A penalty was imposed after tests revealed vitamin levels were below prescribed standards. This rendered the product substandard under the Food Safety and Standards Act. FSSAI did not disclose the specific penalty amount imposed.

items.title: NBFC credit surges 14.4% to ₹59.3 lakh crore in June, retail loans lead growth: RBI data
items.summary: Non-banking finance company credit grew 14.4 percent year-on-year in June. Retail loans saw the fastest expansion, increasing by 20.3 percent. Housing and vehicle loans, and gold jewellery loans showed robust growth. Credit to industry expanded by 6.7 percent, while services sector credit grew 17.6 percent. Agriculture and allied activities credit increased significantly by 17.9 percent.

Enterprise revenue for Ginger stood at ₹301 crore in the first quarter of FY27.

items.title: Oil minister Hardeep Singh Puri dismisses concerns about fuel adulteration
items.summary: Hardeep Singh Puri addressed the issue of fuel adulteration, asserting that concerns over it are baseless. A nationwide investigation uncovered only four instances at various petrol stations. He emphasized that oil marketing firms implement strict testing protocols. Analysis results indicate that chloride levels remain safe and do not support allegations of excessive chloride presence.

items.title: Britannia sees demand rise, but sugar and palm oil costs bite
items.summary: Britannia Industries said consumer demand strengthened in the June quarter, helping revenue rise 9.5% and profit nearly 14% year-on-year. However, rising sugar, palm oil and fuel costs are pressuring margins, prompting the company to consider further pricing measures.

items.title: Handloom's Fashion Reset: Next fillip for India’s handmade textiles must come from the young
items.summary: Younger Indians are showing renewed interest in handloom textiles and their heritage. Social media and "indie" labels are making handloom fabrics fashionable and sustainable. Designers are creatively reinterpreting traditional handloom patterns for modern clothing. This shift brings new understanding and respect for weavers' skills and livelihoods. The future of Indian handloom will be shaped by this younger generation's engagement.

items.title: CBIC directs CGST zones to track illegal mining, curb tax evasion
items.summary: Central tax authorities are taking proactive measures by partnering with state mining departments to address the issue of illegal mineral extraction and transportation. This collaboration will involve setting up a comprehensive information-sharing system across all CGST areas. This directive is a result of a CAG report identifying critical gaps in intelligence sharing, with the goal of significantly reducing tax evasion in the mining sector.

items.title: India weighs friendlier investment treaty rules as Cabinet nod nears: DEA Secretary
items.summary: India is reviewing its bilateral investment treaty model to attract more foreign capital. This review aims to make the treaty more investor-friendly and address existing concerns. Private investments are showing steady growth, benefiting from public capital expenditure increases. The government is also considering relaxing timelines for foreign investors to pursue global arbitration. India seeks to ensure stability and predictability for international capital during global turmoil.

items.summary: The weak job report for July has tempered expectations surrounding a Federal Reserve rate increase. Consequently, futures markets now indicate a diminished probability of a rise in interest rates next month. Despite calls from several Fed officials for tighter monetary policy to counteract inflation, the economic community remains split on what lies ahead in rate decisions. The Federal Reserve is actively tracking inflation trends to shape its future policies.
